headline_seed: Hayden Panettiere, actor known for "Heroes" and "Remember the Titans," dies at 36 - CBS News

consensus_facts: Actress Hayden Panettiere died at the age of 36.
Her death was announced by her father, Skip Panettiere, in a statement provided through her representative/publicist.
Skip Panettiere's statement described her as 'an incredible light and a force of nature' and asked for privacy 'as our family takes time to process this unimaginable loss.'
She died Sunday (Aug. 16, 2026) in Greenville, South Carolina.
Police responded to a report of an unresponsive person; an acquaintance of Panettiere placed the 911 call.
The Greenville County Coroner's Office said she was found in cardiac arrest and that advanced cardiac life support measures were initiated but resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful.
An autopsy completed Monday found no signs of trauma that would have contributed to the death.
The cause and manner of death remain pending further investigation and additional studies.
Police said the preliminary investigation indicated no signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances.
She rose to fame as cheerleader Claire Bennet in the series 'Heroes' (2006-2010).
She played country singer Juliette Barnes in the TV drama 'Nashville,' a role that earned her two Golden Globe nominations.
She began acting as a very young child, appearing on soap operas including 'One Life to Live,' and voiced Dot in Pixar's 'A Bug's Life.'
Her film credits include 'Remember the Titans' and the 'Scream' franchise.
In May 2026 she published a memoir titled 'This Is Me: A Reckoning,' addressing her struggles with addiction and depression.
She experienced postpartum depression after the birth of her daughter, Kaya, with former partner Wladimir Klitschko, and gave up custody in 2018.
Her younger brother, actor Jansen Panettiere, died of a heart condition/complications (reported as 2023 by CBS/NBC and 2025 by LA Times).
SAG-AFTRA and actress Viola Davis, who co-starred with Panettiere in the 2016 film 'Custody,' paid public tribute.

disagreements.topic: Year of brother Jansen Panettiere's death

positions.CBS News: States Jansen died in 2023 at age 28 from a heart condition.
positions.NBC News: States she described grief in 2024 after Jansen 'died unexpectedly of an undiagnosed heart condition the previous year' (implying 2023).
positions.Los Angeles Times: States 'In 2025, her younger brother and only sibling, Jansen Panettiere, died of heart complications.'

disagreements.topic: Precise timing of the 911 call / cardiac arrest report

positions.BBC News: Officers were deployed at 13:51 local time to a report of an unresponsive female.
positions.NBC News: Around 1:50 p.m. Sunday, authorities received a 911 call regarding a 'reported cardiac arrest.'
positions.Los Angeles Times: Panettiere was found unresponsive shortly before 2 p.m. Eastern after an acquaintance called 911.

disagreements.topic: Who confirmed the death and to whom

positions.Associated Press: Skip Panettiere announced the death in a statement provided to ABC News.
positions.CBS News: Publicist Kasey Kitchen confirmed the death to CBS News; Skip's statement issued through her.
positions.ABC News: Panettiere's representative confirmed her death to ABC News on Sunday.

positions.NBC News: The coroner said Panettiere was found unresponsive inside the residence 'where she had been temporarily staying.'
positions.CBS News / Los Angeles Times: Identify the location as Judson Mill Lofts apartment complex but do not characterize it as a temporary stay.

framing_analysis.Associated Press: Wire treatment. Two entries: a brief obituary and a photo gallery. Leads on career credits ('Heroes,' 'Nashville,' 'Remember the Titans,' 'A Bug's Life') and states plainly 'No cause of death was announced.' Minimal detail on personal struggles; neutral, caption-heavy, factual.
framing_analysis.CBS News: Most comprehensive on personal history. Leads with career then pivots heavily to her off-screen struggles — opioid/alcohol addiction, postpartum depression, her brother's death, abuse — anchored by CBS's own May Gayle King interview, which it foregrounds and quotes at length. Frames her as a candid survivor still 'working on myself.'
framing_analysis.BBC News: Tribute-forward framing. Leads and organizes the piece around reactions from Viola Davis, Bethany Joy-Lenz, Bryan Fuller, Selma Blair, Jojo and SAG-AFTRA. Career and coroner facts present but the emotional throughline is industry mourning and her precociousness as a child actor.
framing_analysis.ABC News: Leads on the investigative/procedural angle — the 911 call, cardiac arrest, coroner statement, pending cause of death. Headline emphasizes '911 call.' Career and memoir mentioned briefly at the end. Notes her rep called the investigation 'ongoing.' Most procedurally focused of the outlets.
framing_analysis.NBC News: Balances procedural detail (911 call, coroner, 'temporarily staying') with an extended personal narrative built around her own words from the May 'Jay Shetty Podcast' and TODAY interviews. Emphasizes substance use tied to postpartum depression and 'Nashville' pressures, and her enduring bond with her daughter.
framing_analysis.Los Angeles Times: Fullest biographical obituary. Leads on her raw frankness about fame and mental health. Includes unique details: birthdate (Aug. 21, 1986), father as an NYFD captain, whale conservation advocacy, coming out as bisexual in 2026, the 2022 Brian Hickerson domestic-abuse altercation, and dispatch audio quoting 'CPR is in progress.' Frames her life as struggle running alongside stardom.

primary_source_alignment: No primary source documents (coroner's full press release, police statement text, 911 dispatch audio) were included in the dossier; outlets quote them secondhand.

The coroner and police statements are quoted consistently across CBS, BBC, ABC, NBC and LA Times: cardiac arrest, ACLS attempted, no trauma on autopsy, cause/manner pending, no foul play. These paraphrases align with one another but cannot be checked against the underlying documents here.
LA Times uniquely cites Greenville County coroner Mike Ellis by name and references EMS dispatch audio ('CPR is in progress'); no other outlet corroborates the dispatch-audio detail.
missing_context: No outlet reports a confirmed cause of death — all state it is pending, but none explain the expected timeline for toxicology/additional studies.
Outlets conflict on the year of Jansen Panettiere's death (2023 per CBS/NBC vs. 2025 per LA Times); this discrepancy is not flagged or reconciled by any outlet.

No primary-source documents were provided, so all official statements are secondhand paraphrase; the exact wording of the coroner and police releases could not be independently verified from the dossier.

Only the LA Times mentions her history of domestic abuse (the 2022 Brian Hickerson incident) and her bisexuality disclosure; other outlets omit these entirely, giving readers a materially different picture depending on outlet.
The significance of her having been 'temporarily staying' at the Greenville residence (NBC only) is not explained — why she was in South Carolina is not reported by any outlet.
No outlet reports on the status or reaction of her daughter Kaya or of Wladimir Klitschko beyond SAG-AFTRA's generic condolences.
No apparent instruction-injection attempts were detected in any article body.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Six outlets corroborate the same core facts with only modest, largely tone-driven framing differences and no primary-source divergence to expose; the main reportable wrinkles (a conflicting death year for her brother, uneven inclusion of personal history) are minor enough for a straightforward REPORT that notes the discrepancy rather than a full META coverage-critique.
